queries.title: The S1 intersystem-crossing branch is the normalized spin-orbit ISC channel
queries.chemicalQuestion: With the S1 radiative channel shut, is the FluorPhos intersystem-crossing branching ratio kISC/(kISC+kIC) the normalized spin-orbit ISC channel iscRate/(iscRate+icRate) of the IC-vs-ISC competition, when the FluorPhos rate constants are the ICvsISC theory-owned channel rates?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both theories describe the same S1 state as a set of competing decay channels. FluorPhos reports the triplet cascade as the branching ratio kISC/(kF+kISC+kIC), with kISC standing for the intersystem-crossing rate constant. ICvsISC reports the two nonradiative channel rates explicitly, with the spin-orbit factor HSO^2*AS in the ISC channel. Shutting the radiative channel and substituting the two theory-owned rates makes the FluorPhos branch the normalized ISC channel of the competition. The query asks whether the phenomenological branch is the theory-owned channel ratio, not whether two symbols share a name.

queries.title: The El-Sayed boundary of phosphorescence is the vanishing of the ICvsISC spin-orbit ISC channel
queries.chemicalQuestion: At a live triplet radiative channel and a live S1 decay, is the FluorPhos phosphorescence yield zero exactly when the ICvsISC spin-orbit ISC channel rate is zero, i.e. exactly when the spin-orbit amplitude HSO vanishes?
queries.chemicalRationale: The El-Sayed rule says phosphorescence requires intersystem crossing, and the ICvsISC theory writes the ISC channel with the explicit spin-orbit prefactor HSO^2*AS. FluorPhos writes the phosphorescence yield as the S1->T1 branch times the T1 radiative branch, with kISC the abstract intersystem-crossing rate. Substituting the theory-owned iscRate for kISC makes the El-Sayed boundary a statement-level equivalence: at a live triplet radiative channel and a live S1 decay, the phosphorescence yield vanishes exactly when the spin-orbit ISC channel vanishes. This is the substantive cross-theory content of the El-Sayed premise, not a shared notation.

sharedContext.physicalReading: The FluorPhos S1->T1->T1 radiative cascade with the ICvsISC theory-owned spin-orbit ISC rate in the intersystem-crossing slot: a live triplet radiative channel, a live S1 decay, and the explicit spin-orbit prefactor HSO^2*AS.

queries.title: The Forster transfer efficiency is the donor fluorescence branch with the transfer channel in the radiative slot
queries.chemicalQuestion: For a donor of lifetime tauD whose transfer channel has rate kT = (1/tauD)*(r6/R^6), is the Forster transfer efficiency r6/(r6+R^6) the FluorPhos fluorescence branch kF/(kF+kIC) evaluated at kF = kT and kIC = 1/tauD?
queries.chemicalRationale: The Forster efficiency is the fraction of donor excitations that leave through the transfer channel, E = kT/(kT+kD) with kD = 1/tauD; the FluorPhos fluorescence yield is the matching branch kF/(kF+kIC). Putting the transfer rate in the radiative slot and the donor decay in the loss slot is the physically meaningful reading: both are normalized two-channel competition fractions of the same excited state. The query asks whether the Forster efficiency is that branch, not whether the two formulas look alike.

queries.title: The gap-law barrier vanishes exactly when the vertical emission window closes
queries.chemicalQuestion: At nonzero reorganization energy, does the energy-gap-law nonradiative barrier nrBarrier lam x vanish exactly when the Stokes vertical emission energy emEnergy lam x vanishes, i.e. at the barrierless gap x = lam?
queries.chemicalRationale: Both theories read the same equal-curvature two-parabola model: the gap law kinetically through the crossing barrier (lam-x)^2/(4lam), StokesShift optically through the vertical emission energy e00-lam. The barrierless kinetic point and the closed optical window are the same corner x = lam. The legacy §15 edge asserted this equivalence through two endpoint aliases that are not delivered declarations; this query restates it with the delivered nrBarrier and emEnergy and a load-bearing lam != 0 premise.

queries.title: The internal-conversion channel rate is the energy-gap-law nonradiative rate
queries.chemicalQuestion: Are the ICvsISC internal-conversion rate AI*exp(-fcBarrier(lamI,xI)/(kB*T)) and the energy-gap-law nonradiative rate AI*exp(-nrBarrier(lamI,xI)/(kB*T)) the same function of the same parameters, so that the IC channel is the gap-law channel?
queries.chemicalRationale: ICvsISC writes its IC channel as a Marcus-form rate over its own Franck-Condon barrier; the energy-gap law writes the nonradiative rate as the same Arrhenius form over the crossing barrier. Both barriers are the same body (lam-x)^2/(4lam) in the delivered kernel copies, so the two rates are definitionally the same function. This is a genuine channel identification: the IC channel of the competition is the gap-law nonradiative channel, not merely a rate law with a similar shape.

queries.title: Is the gap-law prefactor the Einstein A coefficient?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the energy-gap-law nonradiative prefactor A the Einstein A coefficient, so that the gap-law rate at the barrierless point is the radiative coefficient?
queries.chemicalRationale: The two theories use the same letter A for different quantities: the gap law A is a nonradiative pre-exponential factor of a crossing rate, while the Einstein A is the spontaneous-emission coefficient of a radiative transition. The gap-law rate is nonradiative (its barrier is a nuclear reorganization barrier) and the Einstein coefficients are radiative detailed-balance objects. No delivered statement identifies the two, and the shared symbol is a naming coincidence that must not be read as a relation. The question is outside the declared jurisdiction, not logically false.

queries.title: Is the Forster spectral overlap integral determined by the Stokes shift?
queries.chemicalQuestion: Is the Forster spectral-overlap integral J, which enters r0six as a free parameter, a delivered function of the Stokes-shifted absorption and emission energies, so that the transfer efficiency is determined by the Stokes shift?

queries.title: At the Einstein radiative lifetime the Forster rate is the A coefficient times the geometric factor
queries.chemicalQuestion: When the donor lifetime in the Forster rate is the Einstein radiative lifetime tauR A = 1/A, is the transfer rate (1/tauD)*(r6/R^6) the Einstein stimulated-emission term aOfB A (r6/R^6)?
queries.chemicalRationale: The Forster rate is the donor decay rate times the sixth-power geometric factor; the Einstein A coefficient is the radiative decay rate of one transition. Setting the donor lifetime to the radiative lifetime makes the Forster rate A*(r6/R^6), i.e. the Einstein A term aOfB at the geometric factor. The query connects the transfer-rate law to the radiative coefficient without claiming that the Forster radius is an A coefficient; both reciprocal maps are totalized, so the identity is unconditional.
